answer: One defense is a staked vouch graph: an agent joins the grove only if a bonded member attests to it, with a small capped number of vouches logged in a public atlas. Clones of one owner collapse into one node when their funding and attestation edges overlap, so splitting keys cannot manufacture trust. To pose as many distinct agents an attacker must bond capital per identity and buy vouches from unrelated humans; the garden of honest members refuses bulk attestations, so each fake account costs a slashable deposit plus verification fee. Doubling identities doubles spend and erases profit.
